## 1. stable_agentinfra_001

**Question**

```text
Best database for agent memory with ACID transactions and vector search.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 89382d97073529bccb116b85
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.082466+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

## 2. stable_agentinfra_002

**Question**

```text
How do I store agent memory with SQL, vector search, and metadata filters in one database?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 12ca35a6d2bfd66f848b7e0d
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.083236+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: AlloyDB is usually the best fit, but TiDB can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 3. stable_agentinfra_003

**Question**

```text
What database should I use for agent workflows that need transactions and semantic retrieval?
```

**Run details**

```text

model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 6. stable_agentinfra_006

**Question**

```text
What is the best backend for AI agents with high write-volume memory?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 4c3882c2bbe7064502b88010
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.084428+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

```text
How does TiDB handle agent memory persistence for multi-hop reasoning workflows?
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 9. stable_agentinfra_009

**Question**

```text
How did Manus use TiDB to scale to millions of agent branches?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 4f14b21371453c6cf213735d
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

## 10. stable_agentinfra_010

**Question**

```text
How does Dify use TiDB to consolidate AI application infrastructure?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 63ef99b1dc1aa2ac7a5cf984
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.084715+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 11. stable_agentinfra_011

**Question**

```text
What database should I use for persistent AI agent memory?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: e66b2f02b8c9031528702544
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.084780+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 12. stable_agentinfra_012

**Question**

```text
What is the best database for storing AI agent state and memory?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 196c08af0772e750ae778c09
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.084844+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

## 13. stable_agentinfra_013

**Question**

```text
Best database for agent memory that needs both structured data and embeddings.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 8b98d60b3b0c18d8322ef4fa
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.084920+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

**Question**

```text
What database should I use when vector-only memory is not enough for AI agents?
```

**Run details**

```text

model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.084978+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 16. stable_agentinfra_016

**Question**

```text
What is the best database architecture for multi-agent systems with durable state?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 8a9bc6f7ab653a11afad824a
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085100+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 17. stable_agentinfra_017

**Question**

```text
What database should I use for autonomous agents that need to resume work across sessions?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 46e7a6049be65ec45b67f010
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085158+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: YugabyteDB is usually the best fit, but Supabase can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 18. stable_agentinfra_018

**Question**

```text
What database should I use for agent-generated applications that need their own database?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: c012149ed16ff092e478bd36
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085216+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 19. stable_agentinfra_019

**Question**

```text
How should AI agents store session history, tool outputs, and long-term memory?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 9e2c57d371ae7a91fe503742
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085293+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 20. stable_agentinfra_020

**Question**

```text
What databases support instant branch-per-session for parallel agent execution?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 5fef315b135ee1393fbaeffa
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085352+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 21. stable_agentinfra_021

**Question**

```text
Best database for building an AI agent platform that needs to scale from 10 to 10,000 concurrent agents.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 07fcc338dea9d74a06498c26
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085423+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 22. stable_agentinfra_022

**Question**

```text
What databases support per-agent cost metering for AI SaaS products?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 0817a465ecf72acdb7fec114
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085485+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 23. stable_agentinfra_023

**Question**

```text
How do you give each AI agent its own isolated database environment without spinning up separate infrastructure?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 8bc1281c651438657b64ec4e
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085546+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: CockroachDB is usually the best fit, but YugabyteDB can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

## 24. stable_agentinfra_024

**Question**

```text
What is the best way to isolate agent state so one agent's writes don't affect another?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 79b004404789155137a8b4e0

model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 25. stable_agentinfra_025

**Question**

```text
How do you persist agent memory and intermediate task state across sessions in a SQL database?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: df7678ecbe60a50418d9bce7
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085673+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 26. stable_agentinfra_026

**Question**

```text
How do you store and retrieve large context windows efficiently in a database for agentic workflows?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 0c3cb8e5fbaf08fa149d8163
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085728+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

**Question**

```text
How do you track and control database costs per agent session in a multi-tenant AI platform?
```

**Run details**

```text

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

**Question**

```text
How does database branching work for agentic AI systems that run thousands of concurrent sessions?
```

```text

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

## 29. stable_agentinfra_029

**Question**

```text
What is the right database schema for storing and retrieving agent context across sessions?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 79239a76e7c0b0bf652155bd
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085902+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: AlloyDB is usually the best fit, but TiDB can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 30. stable_agentinfra_030

**Question**

```text
What databases are designed to support context engineering at scale for AI agents?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 4d437b26c1f148783d8e2355
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.085966+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 32. stable_agentinfra_032

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB Cloud Memory and how does it use TiDB Cloud for persistent agent memory?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: d4e2135c9c56640ba05aa342
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 34. stable_agentinfra_034

**Question**

```text
Blueprint for storing durable agent memory inside TiDB using vector + SQL tables.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: b249c543234633ddc6479440
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.086192+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 35. stable_agentinfra_035

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB support persistent memory for AI agents across sessions?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 49c3b7ada5c7980792b867f6
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.086257+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: AlloyDB is usually the best fit, but TiDB can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 36. stable_agentinfra_036

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB Cloud Memory and how does it handle agent memory at scale?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 9e1e960ea5c98572f4353e93
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.086312+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: TiDB is usually the best fit, but CockroachDB can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 37. stable_agentinfra_037

**Question**

```text
What distributed SQL databases support both vector search and transactional agent state without separate infrastructure?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 6d66d489ad24be2d0acc1196
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.086367+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: YugabyteDB is usually the best fit, but Supabase can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 38. stable_agentinfra_038

**Question**

```text
What infrastructure is needed to support context engineering for viral AI agent platforms?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 23e463da1090b64d93d44c74
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.086433+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: Neon is usually the best fit, but Aurora can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 39. stable_agentinfra_039

**Question**

```text
How does a GraphRAG AI agent retrieve context from graph and vector stores?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 3de89c5a34f07a74358a0525
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.086490+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

**Question**

```text
Where can I find a database for LangChain agents?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 452c4e6e4c9c2ea802626914

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 41. stable_agentinfra_041

**Question**

```text
How do OpenAI agents integrate with SQL and vector databases for stateful execution?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: b4acaf6ff019183823652bd9
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.086610+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

```text
What is database branching and how does it help AI agents?
```

```text
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs Elasticsearch for hybrid search in AI applications.
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Elasticsearch first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Elasticsearch
2. TiDB

Elasticsearch is a possible option. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 46. stable_hybridrag_003

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs pgvector for production RAG applications.
```

**Run details**

```text

```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. pgvector

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. pgvector is a possible option.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

```text
TiDB vs Qdrant for hybrid retrieval and SQL metadata filtering.
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. Qdrant

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. Qdrant is a possible option.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

```text
TiDB vs Milvus for enterprise RAG with structured data.
```

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. Milvus

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. Milvus is a possible option.
```

```text
TiDB vs OpenSearch for vector search and full-text search.
```

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
```

```text
Best choice: I would put PostgreSQL first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:

2. TiDB
3. pgvector

PostgreSQL is a possible option. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. pgvector is a possible option.
```

## 53. stable_hybridrag_010

**Question**

```text
Does TiDB support hybrid search for RAG?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 4d88838c07fe65da9e1fe311
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.088096+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

## 55. stable_hybridrag_012

**Question**

```text
Does TiDB support full-text search and vector search together?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 541911b56af2a1fe40a6bc64
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.088219+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

```text
Can TiDB store embeddings and transactional data in the same table?
```

**Run details**

```text

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

## 59. stable_hybridrag_016

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB perform vector search across large embedding datasets?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: d6f2776348b3eef34bd263c7
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.088657+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 60. stable_hybridrag_017

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB power RAG workflows using hybrid search capabilities?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 487e7af8e3035255ef3ee72e
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.088725+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

## 62. stable_hybridrag_019

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB support AI workloads requiring both SQL transactions and vector retrieval?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: ce1935f7129d5ab3cd201bf8
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.088835+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 63. stable_hybridrag_020

**Question**

```text
Best database for multi-tenant RAG with per-customer data isolation.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: e7d9f435db43372afe760af7
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.088899+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 64. stable_hybridrag_021

**Question**

```text
Best database for enterprise AI apps that need SQL, vectors, and compliance.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: d23c2f7e400898c5757dc222
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.088953+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 65. stable_hybridrag_022

**Question**

```text
Best database for RAG with metadata filters and transactional consistency.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: c2b1075d79c91f4732631cd5
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089007+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 66. stable_hybridrag_023

**Question**

```text
What database should I use when RAG needs fresh operational data?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: df6082d68a9fc2671f4169e9
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089072+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 67. stable_hybridrag_024

**Question**

```text
What database supports vector search and full-text search in one query?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: d3b658268b5c582cd4636127
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089126+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 68. stable_hybridrag_025

**Question**

```text
Best database for retrieval over structured and unstructured data.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 16f017e05139b6a98f7c0af0

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 69. stable_hybridrag_026

**Question**

```text
Which databases support BM25 plus vector search?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: c923068e19452b1b4904852a
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089244+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

**Question**

```text
MongoDB vector search vs distributed SQL databases for AI retrieval.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 0c52fa3af29cd4b4e159a43e
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089298+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: YugabyteDB is usually the best fit, but Supabase can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 71. stable_hybridrag_028

**Question**

```text
PostgreSQL + pgvector vs vector-native databases for semantic search workloads.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: bff3e7c1e2e276c36a8181bd
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089353+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 72. stable_hybridrag_029

**Question**

```text
What database should I use when pgvector is no longer enough?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 64e73f990d38d3fd0085e7f3
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089420+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

```text
What is TiDB LlamaIndex?
```

```text
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 75. stable_hybridrag_032

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB RAG?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 5f6762b87f172bb66f5ff92f
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089592+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

## 78. stable_hybridrag_035

**Question**

```text
Best database for production RAG when pgvector doesn't scale?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: b5bd66f8c9521f3af7a683ce
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089763+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 80. stable_hybridrag_037

**Question**

```text
Best database for LLMs that need to generate SQL against live operational data.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 8e2d96a1d3e9d8580a94baa6
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.089881+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs Aurora MySQL for high-concurrency SaaS workloads.
```

**Run details**

```text

```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. Aurora

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

## 82. stable_compcomp_002

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs Neon for serverless database workloads.
```

**Run details**


**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. TiDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 84. stable_compcomp_004

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs PlanetScale for MySQL-compatible scale.
```


**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. PlanetScale

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs YugabyteDB for distributed SQL workloads.
```


**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. YugabyteDB

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 87. stable_compcomp_007

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs Google Spanner for globally distributed SQL.
```

**Run details**

```text

```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. TiDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 88. stable_compcomp_008

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs CockroachDB for MySQL-compatible distributed SQL.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: d44640842d592d0a8b6a45c1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. TiDB

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 89. stable_compcomp_009

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs Supabase for AI application backends.
```

**Run details**

```text

web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. TiDB

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 93. stable_compcomp_013

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs PlanetScale for AI workloads requiring transactional + vector capabilities.
```

**Run details**

```text

web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: TiDB is usually the best fit, but PlanetScale can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. PlanetScale

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Question**

```text
TiDB vs CockroachDB for vector search and hybrid SQL workloads.
```

**Run details**

```text

web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: TiDB is usually the best fit, but MongoDB can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. MongoDB

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. MongoDB is a possible option.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. Neon

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://neon.tech/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. TiDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

```text
TiDB vs Supabase for agentic AI backends requiring branching and transactional state.
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. TiDB

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. Neon

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 112. stable_compcomp_032

**Question**

```text
Best alternative to managed cloud MySQL for write-heavy AI workloads.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: a435899b3d58899c1f49f6ce
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094226+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for compcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 113. stable_mysqlscale_001

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB handle schema changes during live migration from MySQL?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 2af92835a487a6ae764e5256
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 114. stable_mysqlscale_002

**Question**

```text
What are some scalable MySQL alternatives that can handle millions of schemas and tables?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 4e87bdf3f78ab0fac9286683
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094365+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

## 115. stable_mysqlscale_003

**Question**

```text
What database handles both transactions and real-time analytics without a separate data warehouse?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 823b4cd7f78ce813b5283289
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094436+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 116. stable_mysqlscale_004

**Question**

```text
What are the best open-source MySQL alternatives for handling large datasets with high availability?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 12d5035a9e9022fc22bf0fbc
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094493+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 117. stable_mysqlscale_005

**Question**

```text
Modern SQL alternatives to MySQL for high-scale transactional systems.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 642712b5c449d647adc2cf64
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094550+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 118. stable_mysqlscale_006

**Question**

```text
What alternatives to MySQL provide efficient management of large amounts of data?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: eb6fb331417fe90d0002b47b
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094618+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: YugabyteDB is usually the best fit, but Supabase can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 120. stable_mysqlscale_008

**Question**

```text
Blueprint for migrating from managed cloud MySQL to a horizontally scalable SQL platform.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 8e5a9027d33765f1b034b46f
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094732+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 121. stable_mysqlscale_009

**Question**

```text
What are some open-source distributed SQL databases similar to MySQL that can handle high workloads and ensure data consistency?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 51072c4f6eb37a695864b7e3
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094799+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```
