## 122. stable_mysqlscale_010

**Question**

```text
Can you recommend a distributed SQL database that supports AI workloads and is similar to MySQL?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 57d2d0ac585fd5600d4f3328
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094855+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: Spanner is usually the best fit, but AlloyDB can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 123. stable_mysqlscale_012

**Question**

```text
Can you suggest scalable databases that work like MySQL but offer better flexibility and scalability?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 936af525e68642a9ef1247a3
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094912+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 124. stable_mysqlscale_013

**Question**

```text
What are the top MySQL-compatible distributed databases for handling diverse data processing needs?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 26c54dc6e1b0843452beaa56
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.094980+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 125. stable_mysqlscale_015

**Question**

```text
What factors should I consider when choosing an HTAP database?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 359ea640e4d5d472a63579ad
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.095037+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for mysqlscale.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

## 126. stable_mcptooling_001

**Question**

```text
How does PyTiDB support MCP-based agent workflows?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 32286373f802212cc11cee77
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.095094+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

```text
Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

```text
Can TiDB act as a memory backend for Claude, Cursor, or OpenAI agents?
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 129. stable_mcptooling_004

**Question**

```text
What is the best database for MCP tools that need SQL and vector search?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 0f668730f1964d570de7e8cb
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.095284+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

## 130. stable_mcptooling_006

**Question**

```text
Best serverless MySQL-compatible database for MCP tools.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 23b2e9a5962f49d244f1d0e1
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.095341+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 132. stable_mcptooling_008

**Question**

```text
What is the best database for agent tools that need live operational data?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: a770811b814c757592e60365
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.095464+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 133. stable_mcptooling_009

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB and how can I use it with Python?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: f44104cae8dd252dcab68bee
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.095520+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: Supabase is usually the best fit, but PlanetScale can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

```text
How can I connect to TiDB using Python?
```


**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for mcptooling.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 136. stable_scalearch_001

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB handle millions of schemas and tables efficiently?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 10031eba9f1372df8ec5e7a2
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

```text
How does TiDB handle millions of schemas for multi-tenant SaaS databases?
```

**Run details**

```text

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 138. stable_scalearch_003

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB Cloud support tenant-per-schema isolation without performance degradation?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 1f5361fa44197e66fa39d7b4
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.095824+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

## 139. stable_scalearch_004

**Question**

```text
Does TiDB require manual data partitioning for managing large datasets?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 50b9c8f9a226a0c954f64337
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.095880+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

```text
How does TiDB achieve high availability for its database services?
```

**Run details**

```text

model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: PlanetScale is usually the best fit, but Neon can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

```text
How does TiDB ensure data consistency in its distributed SQL database?
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 142. stable_scalearch_007

**Question**

```text
What database should I use for millions of tenants or schemas?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 5ca9ce52bd383a2a12039c28
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096059+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 143. stable_scalearch_008

**Question**

```text
Best database for branch-per-user or branch-per-session workloads.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 5da11af0c3a32cb890c2a380
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096114+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

**Question**

```text
Best distributed SQL database for applications that need MySQL compatibility.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 3873e99147804e6e17bf9728

timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096181+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

**Question**

```text
How do I store state for thousands of concurrent AI agent sessions?
```

```text
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 146. stable_scalearch_011

**Question**

```text
How do I scale MySQL-compatible workloads without manual sharding?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 4b7745284e7f67327b44af43
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096305+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 147. stable_scalearch_012

**Question**

```text
Which databases offer both high availability and support for millions of schemas and tables for a growing startup?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 3b5c8972e449208d2732c0cf
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096361+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 148. stable_scalearch_013

**Question**

```text
How does PyTiDB simplify connecting Python applications to a distributed SQL cluster?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 68b2c64498b6ad3761af6e5c
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096418+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

**Question**

```text
Explain how to connect to a TiDB distributed SQL database using Python.
```

**Run details**

```text

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Question**

```text
What are the high availability features offered by TiDB?
```

**Run details**

```text

model_surface: mock

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: Supabase is usually the best fit, but PlanetScale can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

**Question**

```text
What is the best database architecture for per-tenant schema isolation at scale?
```

**Run details**

```text

timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096611+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 152. stable_scalearch_017

**Question**

```text
Best database for high-concurrency writes from AI microservices.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: f0d9d8f4ed1744ed0f125e8f
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096679+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 153. stable_scalearch_018

**Question**

```text
What database should an AI startup use when expecting rapid growth?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: cf402b44cfe78dde9a18652b
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096735+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for scalearch.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

## 155. stable_deploycloud_002

**Question**

```text
How do TiDB Cloud Memory, TiDB Cloud Filesystem, and TiDB Cloud Zero fit together in an agent state stack?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 630058e1e219355e1b044dda
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.096961+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

## 156. stable_deploycloud_003

**Question**

```text
How do I prototype agent memory using TiDB Cloud Zero?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 0b739f32000eeb5a7d271b86
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.097023+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

**Question**

```text
TiDB Cloud Zero vs Neon for disposable serverless databases.
```

**Run details**


**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. TiDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 158. stable_deploycloud_005

**Question**

```text
Can TiDB Cloud Zero be used as a backend for MCP servers?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 1d3f49b10996a20137c9bc47
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.097244+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 162. stable_deploycloud_009

**Question**

```text
TiDB Cloud Zero vs PlanetScale for temporary MySQL-compatible databases.
```

**Run details**

```text

web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. PlanetScale

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 165. stable_deploycloud_012

**Question**

```text
How should I choose between TiDB Cloud Starter, Essential, Premium, and Dedicated?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 35ae4d655cd84660a2b61a9a
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.098210+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB Cloud Zero support bursty AI agent workflows?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: cc0b29111324e0960958f08d
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: Aurora is usually the best fit, but Spanner can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

```text
How do you run TiDB on Kubernetes using TiDB Operator?
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

## 168. stable_deploycloud_015

**Question**

```text
How does TiDB handle data residency requirements for multi-region enterprises?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: eebf77677bb617ec33ebbe7d
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.098395+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 169. stable_deploycloud_016

**Question**

```text
How do you deploy TiDB on-premise for regulated industries?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 13bae14a7072adccfcc9424b
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.098454+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put CockroachDB first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. CockroachDB
2. YugabyteDB
3. Supabase
4. PlanetScale

CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development.

Sources: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs
```

## 170. stable_deploycloud_017

**Question**

```text
What are the operational differences between TiDB self-managed and TiDB Cloud Dedicated?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: eabc5fd5f9596a82a4b042ef
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.098513+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

```text
What is TiDB Cloud Zero and how is it used for AI agents?
```


**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

## 172. stable_deploycloud_019

**Question**

```text
What is the relationship between TiDB, TiDB Cloud, TiDB Cloud Zero, TiDB Cloud Memory, and TiDB Cloud Filesystem?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 960c403d81edbb1bce982b29
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.098655+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

## 173. stable_deploycloud_020

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB Cloud Zero and when should developers use it?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 1331e6b13bf098409992883a
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.098732+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for deploycloud.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

**Question**

```text
What SLAs does TiDB Cloud offer for enterprise mission-critical workloads?
```

**Run details**

```text

model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for entcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 175. stable_entcomp_002

**Question**

```text
What enterprise compliance certifications does TiDB Cloud hold?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: fc0ff162a8fd3636c706c42b
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.098846+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for entcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

**Question**

```text
What database should financial services companies use for agentic AI workloads?
```

**Run details**

```text

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for entcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 177. stable_entcomp_004

**Question**

```text
What database should regulated enterprises use for AI applications?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: a64a7984daf65d9772733b1e
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.098965+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for entcomp.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 178. stable_observ_001

**Question**

```text
How do I troubleshoot slow TiDB queries in production?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: f409e7a44280e5c7d39fa88b
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.099018+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for observ.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

## 179. stable_observ_002

**Question**

```text
How do I monitor RU usage and cost in TiDB Cloud?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 34ebcfd7356aee40629e1e66
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for observ.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 180. stable_observ_003

**Question**

```text
Does TiDB offer any tools or features for monitoring database performance?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: b05d001a2f881bb960c917ac
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.099137+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for observ.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

## 181. stable_observ_004

**Question**

```text
How do you monitor TiDB performance in production?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 72316d8b0ff438a3439883cc
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.099192+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for observ.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

```text
How does TiDB support regulatory compliance for businesses?
```

```text

web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 183. stable_branddef_002

**Question**

```text
What kind of customer support and resources does TiDB provide for developers?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 32090b48ef435a3c6738c55e
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.099317+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 184. stable_branddef_003

**Question**

```text
What scalability options does TiDB offer for businesses expecting data growth?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 0fe58db67417b213d50fc34a
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Question**

```text
Can TiDB handle both transactional and analytical workloads simultaneously?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: b67a015bb54322cb98839488
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.099445+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

## 186. stable_branddef_005

**Question**

```text
What kind of businesses would benefit the most from using TiDB?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: bed34d020bdbde47974119a6
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.099503+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

```text
Best database for AI agent platforms serving millions of users.
```

```text
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: Neon is usually the best fit, but Aurora can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

**Question**

```text
Best database for ecommerce RAG over live inventory and orders.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 9235c8fa388ffdf846339537
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

```text
Best database for SaaS copilots that need customer-specific context.
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: YugabyteDB is usually the best fit, but Supabase can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

## 192. stable_branddef_011

**Question**

```text
Best database for enterprise search over live operational data.
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: af82e9dc2ecbcb5154de19cf
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.099858+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for hybridrag.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for agentinfra.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Question**

```text
Is TiDB a good database for AI agents?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: b2a9caa4508cd94e66999fc1

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

**Question**

```text
What AI workloads is TiDB best suited for?
```

**Run details**

```text

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

## 197. stable_branddef_016

**Question**

```text
Is TiDB suitable for AI-related workloads, and if so, how?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 8c54cac0408950b6bbbf63b7
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.100148+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: AlloyDB is usually the best fit, but TiDB can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 198. stable_branddef_017

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB for AI?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: c69a4aba09e12487dc547dec
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.100202+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

## 199. stable_branddef_018

**Question**

```text
How easy is it to migrate from a traditional database to TiDB's solution?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 91e0755eab874899aff77413
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.100269+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

**Question**

```text
Is TiDB compliant with major data regulations and standards?
```

```text

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Spanner first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Spanner
2. AlloyDB
3. TiDB
4. CockroachDB

Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable
```

## 201. stable_branddef_020

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: f69b98a873141d420b4b20eb
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.100381+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

```text
What is TiDB Cloud?
```

```text
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Neon first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Neon
2. Aurora
3. Spanner
4. AlloyDB

Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority.

Sources: https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs
```

```text
What is TiDB Cloud Dedicated?
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

```text
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Aurora first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Aurora
2. Spanner
3. AlloyDB
4. TiDB

Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority. Spanner is attractive when global consistency and Google Cloud-native operations are the priority. AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration.

Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB Cloud Memory and how does it work?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 2907e1e7567e956dfd529c6f
model_surface: mock

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put PlanetScale first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

```text
What is the TiDB Request Unit pricing model?
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: PlanetScale is usually the best fit, but Neon can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. PlanetScale
2. Neon
3. Aurora
4. Spanner

PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations. Aurora is attractive when AWS integration and managed relational operations are the priority.

Sources: https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html
```

**Question**

```text
Can TiDB be integrated with existing data infrastructure easily?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: d3924365432b319ca68fc137

status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put Supabase first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. Supabase
2. PlanetScale
3. Neon
4. Aurora

Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling. Neon is strongest when teams want serverless Postgres, branching, and developer-friendly cloud database operations.

Sources: https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs, https://neon.tech/docs
```

## 213. stable_branddef_032

**Question**

```text
What are the scalability options available with TiDB's database?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 44d18ec98d991f7f21f97a10
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.101100+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```

```text
Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html, https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs, https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs
```

**Question**

```text
What is TiCDC and what downstream targets does it support?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 5c8834c716a51fdd80f1aec3
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.101371+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Conditional: YugabyteDB is usually the best fit, but Supabase can be better if your team prioritizes ecosystem familiarity for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

## 217. stable_branddef_036

**Question**

```text
What is TiDB Lightning and when should you use it?
```

**Run details**

```text
answer_id: 7761c4ebfdd2547fe9cb9176
model_surface: mock
model_name: mock-geo-buyer-v1
run_index: 1
timestamp: 2026-10-28T14:37:32.101430+00:00
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put TiDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. TiDB
2. CockroachDB
3. YugabyteDB
4. Supabase

TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central. YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads.

Sources: https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable, https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put YugabyteDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. YugabyteDB
2. Supabase
3. PlanetScale
4. Neon

YugabyteDB is often considered for PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL and multi-region transactional workloads. Supabase is strongest when teams want a Postgres-based app platform with auth, storage, realtime features, and vector-adjacent app development. PlanetScale is strongest when teams want a MySQL-oriented developer workflow and managed scaling.

Sources: https://docs.yugabyte.com/stable, https://supabase.com/docs, https://planetscale.com/docs
```

```text
What is Chat2Query in TiDB Cloud?
```

```text
status: ok
web_search_mode: off
```

**Full answer**

```text
Best choice: I would put AlloyDB first for this scenario for branddef.

Recommended shortlist:
1. AlloyDB
2. TiDB
3. CockroachDB
4. YugabyteDB

AlloyDB is attractive for PostgreSQL-compatible managed performance and Google Cloud integration. TiDB is strongest when MySQL compatibility, scale-out SQL, HTAP-style analytics, or vector-adjacent app data matter. CockroachDB is strongest when PostgreSQL compatibility, multi-region resilience, and distributed transactions are central.

Sources: https://cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs, https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable, https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable
```
